title: Consolidate lint profiles and introduce zero-state presubmit bootstrap
author: Aisha Menon
description: Summary: Consolidates multiple, overlapping lint profiles into a small set of stage-aware profiles and introduces a zero-state presubmit bootstrap that makes presubmit runs meaningful on cold CI workers. Motivation: We observed long, noisy presubmit runs and duplicated lint config across the monorepo: duplicate eslint/ruff/clang-tidy settings, per-package overrides that differed only by naming, and expensive full-toolchain setup on ephemeral builders. This PR reduces presubmit noise, speeds cold-start feedback, and makes CI more deterministic without changing lint rules themselves. Goals: 1) Reduce presubmit setup time on freshly provisioned runners by ~40-60% via a lightweight zero-state bootstrap; 2) Replace ad-hoc per-package lint manifests with three canonical profiles (fast, standard, strict) and a small plugin adapter that maps legacy package settings to profiles; 3) Add a rollback-safe release gate: if a staged release pipeline sees presubmit regressions, the rollout will automatically pause and fall back to the previous artifact. Checklist: - [x] Introduce canonical lint profiles and a profile mapper for legacy packages - [x] Implement zero-state bootstrap that downloads only minimal toolchain artifacts and warms caches in parallel - [x] Add lightweight presubmit telemetry (duration, cold-start flag, cache-hit rate) - [x] Update devcontainer and CONTRIBUTING to document profile selection - [x] Add rollback safeguard to release orchestration and a short-circuit in the deployer - [x] E2E smoke job for fast presubmit lane added to nightly to ensure zero-state health Design notes: - Profiles: fast (lint-only + quick type checks), standard (full suite excluding slow integration checks), strict (standard + extra static analysis steps used for release candidates). - Zero-state bootstrap: a small shim (bash/Go) that validates and fetches a minimal toolchain image manifest, fetches cached wheels/archives in parallel, primes node/yarn caches with core deps, and extracts prebuilt binaries for common linters. The shim emits a cold-start metric that is consumed by the presubmit telemetry service. - Profile mapper: lightweight YAML transforms that map legacy per-package config into one of the three canonical profiles; this avoids touchy code changes in language-specific configs while keeping behavior intact. - Rollback safeguard: release pipeline checks presubmit telemetry for spike in cold-start failures or increase in lint failures vs baseline; on breach, the orchestrator pauses rollout and notifies the release lead with a one-click rollback. Why this is different: previous PRs trimmed CI matrices and split lint shards; this PR focuses on making presubmit runs robust on cold runners and eliminating profile drift across dozens of packages, rather than only optimizing cache keys. Backwards compatibility: The mapper preserves existing lint rules; strict profile is opt-in for packages that explicitly request extra checks. Migration: a single codemod (scripts/convert-legacy-lint.sh) updates package manifests to reference profile names; the mapper acts as a compatibility layer while teams migrate incrementally. Risks and mitigations: - Risk: missed package-specific overrides cause unexpected lint behavior. Mitigation: mapper includes a per-package exceptions list and we added an integration test that verifies mapped commands match prior invocations for a sample of 120 packages. - Risk: rollout pause could block urgent releases. Mitigation: release lead can override pause with documented manual gating and the gate auto-expires after 30 minutes with an audit log. Rollout plan: 1) Deploy profiles and mapper to CI and enable fast profile by default for non-release branches. 2) Enable zero-state bootstrap for fast presubmit lane for 48h and compare cold-start telemetry to baseline. 3) Gradually enable zero-state for standard lane and monitor nightly smoke job. 4) After two weeks and stable telemetry, enable rollback safeguard for canary release lane only, then full rollout. Related: ENG-1834 (presubmit stability), ENG-2042 (release rollback tooling).

release_notes: Introduces a zero-state presubmit bootstrap to speed cold CI feedback, consolidates lint profiles into fast/standard/strict, adds a mapper for legacy package configs, and adds a rollback-safe gate for releases that inspects presubmit telemetry. No lint rule changes are included; teams can opt into strict profile for release candidates.
